technology_name: Multi-Criteria Decision System for Streamlining Urban Mobility
institution: KSCSTE - National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC)
problem_solved: Massive operational losses in state transit systems (e.g., KSRTC) caused by uneconomical routes, low network navigability, and a lack of dynamic demand-responsive scheduling.
description: A multi-criteria, graph-theoretical optimization system that models public transit networks as weighted directed graphs. The system incorporates inter-stop spatial distances and real-time Electronic Ticket Machine (ETM) passenger flow data into a weight matrix. It runs advanced topological centrality measures to pinpoint critical transit hubs, map structural redundancy, and optimize route frequencies, bypass options, and dynamic headways.
applications:
• State and municipal road transport corporations (e.g., KSRTC) for route restructuring

• Smart City command centers for dynamic traffic and transit management

• Urban planning consulting firms designing future public transport networks

• Private fleet operators and logistics companies looking for routing efficiency
